'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Eastern Ukraine campaign]]
***The [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Russian Defense Ministry]] claims that [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] have captured the villages of [[Mykolaivka, Novohrodivka urban hromada, Pokrovsk Raion, Donetsk Oblast|Mykolaivka]] and [[Serebrianka, Donetsk Oblast|Serebrianka]] in [[Donetsk Oblast]], while Ukrainian military newspage [[DeepStateMap.Live|DeepState]] reports heavy conflict surrounding [[Selydove]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-forces-capture-two-villages-eastern-ukraine-kyiv-acknowledges-russian-2024-10-24/ (Reuters)]
**[[Foreign involvement in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***The [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] reports that it has confirmed evidence that [[Korean People's Army|North Korean troops]] are now present in [[Russia]] and are preparing to travel to the battlefield in [[Ukraine]]. [[South Korea]] says that [[Pyongyang]] has promised to send up to 10,000 troops to support the war effort. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/23/us-evidence-north-korea-troops-russia-ukraine (''The Guardian'')]
**[[United States and the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***The [[United States Department of Defense|U.S. Defense Department]] finalizes a US$20 billion loan to [[Ukraine]] for military and economic support as part of a collective US$50 billion loan between [[G7]] members. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/us-govt-wants-half-its-20-bln-loan-ukraine-be-military-aid-2024-10-23/ (Reuters)]
*[[Kurdish–Turkish conflict]]
**[[2024 Turkish Aerospace Industries headquarters attack]]
***Five people are killed and 22 more injured during a bombing–shooting attack at the [[Turkish Aerospace Industries]] [[headquarters]] in [[Kahramankazan]], [[Ankara Province]], [[Turkey]]. The perpetrators are later killed during a [[shootout]] with security forces. The [[Government of Turkey|Turkish government]] suspects the [[Kurdistan Workers' Party]] (PKK) to be behind the attack. [https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2024/10/explosion-rocks-turkeys-defense-industry-complex-ankara (Al-Monitor)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/blast-turkish-aviation-company-tusas-hq-gunfire-heard-media-2024-10-23/ (Reuters)] [https://www.dw.com/en/terrorist-attack-hits-turkish-aerospace-firm-near-ankara/a-70580174 (DW)]
***The [[Turkish Air Force]] launches [[airstrike]]s on PKK targets across northern [[Syria]] and [[Iraqi Kurdistan]] in response to the attack, with Turkish [[drone warfare|drone strikes]] in [[Kobani]], Syria, injuring three [[Asayish (North and East Syria)|Asayish]] officers. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkey-hits-pkk-targets-northern-iraq-syria-after-deadly-attack-ankara-2024-10-23/ (Reuters)] [https://hawarnews.com/en/3-members-of-security-forces-wounded-in-turkish-shelling-on-kobani (ANHA)]
*[[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
**[[Assassination of Hashem Safieddine]]
***[[Hezbollah]] confirms that [[Hashem Safieddine]], head of their executive council, was killed in an [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli]] airstrike in [[Beirut]], [[Lebanon]], on October 3. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm242380133o (BBC News)]
*[[Gaza war]]
**Israeli airstrikes across the [[Gaza Strip]] reportedly kill at least 42 people. [[UNRWA]] says one of their staff members was killed after their vehicle was hit by Israeli forces in [[Deir al-Balah]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-steps-up-pressure-northern-gaza-16-killed-across-territory-2024-10-23/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**Nineteen suspected cartel members are killed and one local cartel leader is arrested in a shootout between gunmen and [[National Guard (Mexico)|police officers]] in [[Culiacan]], [[Sinaloa]], [[Mexico]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/shootout-mexicos-sinaloa-state-claims-19-lives-cartel-leader-arrested-2024-10-23/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Two people are killed and 11 injured after an explosion at a [[Toyota Material Handling]] factory in [[Bologna]], [[Italy]]. [https://www.statoquotidiano.it/24/10/2024/bologna-chi-erano-i-due-operai-morti-nellesplosione-alla-toyota/1146207/ (Stato Quotidiano)]
*Three people are found deceased and seven are hospitalized due to [[carbon monoxide poisoning]] at a [[Nursing home|care home]] in [[Swanage]], [[Dorset]], [[England]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/swanage-care-home-deaths-latest-police-giving-update-after-three-die-in-unexplained-care-home-incident-13239573 (Sky News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Demographics of Germany]], [[German economic crisis (2022–present)|German economic crisis]]
**The [[Ifo Institute for Economic Research]] reports that [[Germany]] experienced a 13% [[birth rate]] decline nationally and up to a 17.5% birth rate decline in [[New states of Germany|eastern Germany]] between 2021 and 2023, with the institute attributing the decline to several reasons including the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany|COVID-19 pandemic]], the [[Russo-Ukrainian war]], and [[2021–2023 inflation surge|high inflation]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/german-birth-rate-drops-rapidly-new-report-says/a-70573468 (DW)]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–Holy See relations]]
**[[China]] and the [[Holy See]] agree to extend their [[China–Holy See relations#2018 Holy See–China agreement|2018 provisional agreement]] on the appointment of [[Catholic]] [[bishop]]s in China for a further four years. [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/vatican-city/news/2024-10/holy-see-china-provisional-agreement-appointment-bishops-extend.html (Vatican News)]
*[[China–India relations]]
**[[Prime Minister of India]] [[Narendra Modi]] holds a bilateral meeting with [[President of China]] [[Xi Jinping]] on the sidelines of the [[16th BRICS summit]] in [[Kazan]], [[Russia]]. This is the first bilateral meeting between India and China in five years and comes in the aftermath of the [[2020–2021 China–India skirmishes|2020 border skirmishes between Indian and Chinese troops]]. [https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/brics-summit-prime-minister-narendra-modi-china-xi-jinping-bilateral-talks-russia-lac-disengagement-agreement-2621599-2024-10-23 (India Today)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024 social unrest in Martinique]]
**Protesters with automatic weapons target police and firefighters in [[Martinique]], where protests over the high cost of living have prompted [[France]] to deploy forces to the island. [https://apnews.com/article/martinique-violent-protests-a877760da839735fa92030e1435bdfb4 (AP)]
*A court in [[Munich]], [[Germany]], charges a [[Russians|Russian]] man for stabbing two [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian soldiers]] at a [[shopping center]] in [[Murnau am Staffelsee]], [[Bavaria]], Germany, in April. [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-russian-charged-over-killing-of-ukrainian-soldiers/a-70579206 (DW)]
*A man kills two of his relatives and wounds two more during a [[mass shooting]] at their home in [[Novo Hamburgo]], [[Rio Grande do Sul]], [[Brazil]]. A policeman and the perpetrator are killed during the ensuing [[shootout]], while three more officers are wounded. [https://brazilian.report/liveblog/politics-insider/2024/10/23/shooter-3-dead-9-wounded-firefight/ (The Brazilian Report)]
*[[Prime Minister of Norway|Norwegian Prime Minister]] [[Jonas Gahr Støre]] announces that his government will raise the minimum age limit to use [[social media]] from 13 to 15 in order to protect children from the "power of the algorithms". [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/23/norway-to-increase-minimum-age-limit-on-social-media-to-15-to-protect-children (''The Guardian'')]
